solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pal I associated with tot Chris somehow, e.g. C. Robin

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unspecified way, not in the order printed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's playmate is linked with a toddler called Chris, much like Christopher Robin and his friends.
explanation.walkthrough: An ARCTOPHILIST is a collector or lover of teddy bears; Christopher Robin, owner of Winnie-the-Pooh, is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Robin, the boy devoted to his teddy Pooh, serves as an instance of a teddy-bear enthusiast.

clue.text: Hooligan that is found under gutter, block knocked off?

indicators.note: block is slang for head, so knocking it off removes the opening letter of the word
in a down entry, a piece found under another is written after it

blocks.note: a trough is a channel or gutter
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A thug is spotted lying in the gutter after someone knocked his head off in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: TROUGH loses its head to give ROUGH, and IE goes beneath it to make ROUGHIE. To knock someone's block off is to hit them very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughie is Australian and dialect slang for a rough, violent young man or lout.

clue.text: Company imbibing something with gin in a jiffy

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the first word takes the next one inside it

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
Italian vermouth, drunk in a gin and it

explanation.surface: A firm's staff knock back cocktails very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is Italian vermouth, as in the old bar order gin and it. CITO is Latin, used in English for quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cito is the Latin adverb meaning swiftly, still used in English for doing something speedily.

clue.text: Native Americans confused with Hopi etc

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their original order

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: One tribe is mixed up with the Hopi and others.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hopi are a real tribe, so the surface stays in the scene. OTCHIPWE is a variant name for the Ojibwa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Otchipwe, better known as Ojibwa or Chippewa, are an Algonquian people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Snobbish but not completely, a matter for regret

indicators.note: but not means except, so the word that follows is taken out

blocks.note: uppity means arrogant or self-important
up means completely, as in eat up or used up

explanation.surface: Someone being only half a snob is something to be sorry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' looks like a hint to cut a letter off the end; in fact completely is UP, removed whole from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A pity is something unfortunate that makes one feel sorry, as in it's a pity you missed it.

clue.text: Big bags, passe in colleges

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: passé means out of date
halls are colleges or halls of residence

explanation.surface: Large luggage bags are considered unfashionable at universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Holdalls are large soft travelling bags with room for almost everything one carries.

clue.text: Hazel's bits, tons seized by Leo, causing wailing

indicators.note: things seized by something are gripped and held inside it

blocks.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
amenta are catkins, the hanging flower spikes of hazel
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A lion called Leo grabs hazel twigs and heavy loads, making someone cry out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel's catkins are botanically amenta (singular amentum); Leo is the zodiac lion, and it is split open to hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentation is loud expression of grief, the noun matching wailing as a cry of sorrow.

clue.text: Second-year student in theological college, missing second half

indicators.note: missing its second half means only the opening portion of the word survives

blocks.note: a seminary trains priests

explanation.surface: A student in their second year at a training college for priests is absent for half the term.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI is short for semi-bajan, a second-year student at older Scottish universities such as St Andrews.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish university slang a semi, from semi-bajan, is a student in the second year of study.

clue.text: Trickster that was displaying range in turn of work

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: reach is range or extent
a tour is a spell of duty, as in tour of duty

explanation.surface: A con man shows how far he can go during his shift at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That was' marks the word as obsolete: TREACHOUR is an old form of treacher, a traitor or cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachour is an archaic word for a deceiver or traitor, so a trickster of former times.

clue.text: Insinuate love in writing

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
fist is an old word for handwriting

explanation.surface: Someone hints at affection in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: FIST meaning handwriting is the uncommon sense; love is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist is to slip something in surreptitiously or unwarrantedly, close to insinuating it.

clue.text: Internal inflammation: chloride is restricting whistling sound with one

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so these words enclose the following ones
with simply adds the next piece alongside

blocks.note: common salt is sodium chloride, followed by is as written
a ping is a short high-pitched sound
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A medical note links an inflammation to chloride stifling a wheezing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Chloride stands for common salt, sodium chloride; the restricting is done by the two words together, split after their third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Salpingitis is inflammation of the Fallopian or Eustachian tubes, an inflammation inside the body.

clue.text: Perrier once that has orange mixed in it

indicators.note: mixed letters are stirred out of their printed order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bottle of fizzy mineral water once had orange juice blended into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Perrier looks like the mineral water brand, but a perrier was a medieval stone-throwing engine.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager was an ancient siege catapult that hurled stones, just as a perrier did in medieval warfare.

clue.text: Red wine, sensational, adult quaffed

indicators.note: something quaffed is swallowed, so it ends up inside the other word

blocks.note: gamy can mean racy or scandalous
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up drank a wonderful glass of red.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamay is a black grape of Beaujolais and the light red wine made from it.

clue.text: Dark blue adroitness to surpass in play?

blocks.note: dark blue is Oxford's colour, so Oxford University, OU
tact is skill in handling people

explanation.surface: An Oxford sportsman's skill lets him beat his rivals in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dark Blue is an Oxford University sportsman (Cambridge are the Light Blues).
explanation.definitionFit: To outact is to perform better than a fellow actor, beating them on stage in a play.

clue.text: Lively dance? Not bad for priest abroad

indicators.note: not tells us the following word must be left out

blocks.note: the lambada is a fast Brazilian dance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance that isn't bad suits a clergyman from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not bad' reads as mild praise, but BAD is literally cut out of LAMBADA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a priest of a foreign faith.

clue.text: It's a claim that's silly being addicted to faddish ideas?

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so the letters are put into disarray

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a statement as foolish because it follows passing trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Ismatical describes someone devoted to isms, fashionable doctrines or theories followed slavishly.

clue.text: Certain interference in constellation, a watery condition

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: Hydra, the water snake, is a constellation
electromagnetic interference is a particular kind, abbreviated EMI

explanation.surface: Radio static is disrupting observation of a star group, leaving things damp.
explanation.walkthrough: Hydra is the largest constellation; EMI is electromagnetic interference.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydremia (hydraemia) is a state of the blood having an excess of water, a watery medical condition.

clue.text: Bird limps back to front

indicators.note: back to front says the final letter is carried round to the start

blocks.note: to hop is to move unevenly on one leg

explanation.surface: A wounded bird hobbles along backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is prison time (rhyming slang birdlime, time); Chambers gives SHOP as slang for a prison. 'Back to front' does not reverse the word; it moves its back letter to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for prison: doing bird means serving time, and shop is an old slang word for jail.

clue.text: Wearing royal headgear, acted to contain an ancient township

indicators.note: to contain means to hold within, so the first word surrounds the rest

blocks.note: did means performed or acted
the article
a deme was a township of ancient Attica

explanation.surface: A crowned monarch played the part of ruler of an old Greek town.
explanation.walkthrough: A DEME is a district or township of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Diademed means adorned with a diadem, the jewelled crown or band worn by royalty.

clue.text: Antiseptic, see, turned up in portions

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Dettol is a British brand of antiseptic liquid
la is an old exclamation meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Disinfectant is found in rationed amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: DETTOL is a household antiseptic in Britain; LA is an archaic 'lo!' or 'see!'. Both are reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Allotted means shared out or distributed, given out to each person as a set portion.

clue.text: One after dealers imprisoned by monarchy

indicators.note: imprisoned by means locked inside, so the letters sit within the next word

blocks.note: the inner letters of this word

explanation.surface: An agent pursuing traffickers is locked up by the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: Dealers are drug dealers; NARC is US slang for a narcotics agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A narc is a narcotics officer whose job is to chase down and arrest those who sell drugs.

clue.text: Low-dose contraceptive I pinch inside grinder

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the following word

blocks.note: a mill grinds grain or pepper
taken as written
to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: Someone pinches a mild birth-control tablet and puts it through a grinder.
explanation.definitionFit: The minipill is an oral contraceptive containing a small amount of progestogen only, hence low-dose.

clue.text: Trees dad's planted round another one child removed

indicators.note: removed tells us a piece is taken away from the word before it
planted round means set around, so the first piece encloses the next

blocks.note: pop is dad, with the possessive S
another tree, the larch
ch. is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Father planted trees around a different sort of tree after his son dug it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another one' points back to trees: it means a second kind of tree, which loses the child abbreviation before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplars are tall fast-growing trees of the willow family, often planted in rows.

clue.text: Portion of ground I dug ruined

indicators.note: a portion of is just part of the words that follow

blocks.note: spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A gardener says the patch they dug over was spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Undid can mean brought to ruin or destroyed, as in a scandal undid him.

clue.text: Euro we Scots will go after completely gripped by conflict

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the word that follows
will go after places the first piece at the end of the rest

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
all means wholly
oo is the Scots word for we

explanation.surface: Scottish voices complain that the single currency is caught up in war.
explanation.walkthrough: Euro looks like the currency, but a euro is also a kind of kangaroo, the wallaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the common wallaroo, a large stocky kangaroo of rocky Australian hills.

clue.text: Criminal guild from east and north in dress

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: to tog is to dress, as in togged up
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An oriental gang from the north and east wears a particular outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From east' belongs to the definition, describing the Chinese origin, rather than being a direction to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A tong is a Chinese secret society, often associated with organised crime, so an eastern criminal fraternity.

clue.text: Ban some catapults

indicators.note: some means only part of the following word

blocks.note: the inner letters of this word

explanation.surface: Catapults are partly prohibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapu is the Maori form of taboo, a sacred prohibition or ban placed on something.

clue.text: Oriental without a name, fellow that's very hard up

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letters are dropped

blocks.note: an Indian is from the East
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: An anonymous man from the East is extremely poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means destitute or needy, lacking the means to live, so very short of money.

clue.text: Failure just after being backed repeatedly

indicators.note: being backed means sent back, so the letters read the other way

blocks.note: on means just after, as in on arrival
repeatedly asks for the previous piece once more

explanation.surface: A horse lost right after being supported again and again by punters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles the piece before it is reversed. A no-no is written here without its hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives a no-no as a failure or non-starter, something that cannot succeed.

clue.text: What'll sound like votes against head

indicators.note: sound like tells us the answer is pronounced like the next words

blocks.note: nays are votes of no

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what will be heard as a chorus of no-votes against the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Head is a headland here, not a leader; the Naze is a headland in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: A naze is a headland or promontory, the land jutting into the sea at a ness.

clue.text: Heater turned up? It's a gamble

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an etna is a small spirit lamp for heating liquids

explanation.surface: Turning up the heating is a risky bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Heater looks general, but an etna is a specific small spirit heater named after the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake put into a poker pot before cards are dealt, the money one gambles.

clue.text: Fond couple displaying reverse of prudence mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes
the reverse of a word is that word read backwards

blocks.note: metis is Greek for wisdom or prudence, a word in Chambers

explanation.surface: A loving pair act rashly, showing the opposite of good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: METIS (prudence, cunning) loses its S and is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are an item are a romantic couple openly involved with each other.

clue.text: Spreading ailanto I trimmed, not scaled

indicators.note: trimmed means cut away, so the letter named is removed
spreading things out disturbs their order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ailanto or tree of heaven, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener lops a sprawling tree of heaven, which wasn't climbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scaled' suggests climbing; here it means written in a musical scale or key.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is not written in any key, so it is not organised around a major or minor scale.

clue.text: Like a silky old dress? Far away from famous range

indicators.note: away means gone, so the word before it is taken off

blocks.note: farandine was an old fabric of silk mixed with wool or hair
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shimmering old frock comes from a mountain range a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far away' reads as distant, but FAR is literally taken away from FARANDINE, the old silk-and-wool cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Andine is an adjective meaning of the Andes, the great South American mountain chain.

clue.text: Lobby the upper classes in need of introduction

indicators.note: needing an introduction means lacking its opening letter

blocks.note: the gentry are the landed class below the nobility

explanation.surface: The posh set waiting in a hallway need to be presented to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an entrance hall or passage, the same as a lobby inside a front door.

clue.text: Dreadfully sodden spiels showing unbalanced quality

indicators.note: dreadfully means very badly, so the letters are set down in a poor muddle

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Waterlogged, rambling speeches are terribly skewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopsidedness is the condition of leaning to one side, a lack of balance or symmetry.
